answer: Sybil resistance holds only while a new identity costs more than it can earn before audit. Two conditions enforce that: each vertex in the identity graph must post a scarce, non-fungible proof, one attested enclave plus one staked bond, making bulk registration expensive; and reputation mints solely from unpredictable work, with a zephyr-scheduled audit drawn at random from the nebula of live peers, so farms cannot pre-farm trust or guess which account gets checked.
